title: Daily English — 2026-09-09

grammar.title: Participle Clauses: 문장을 압축하되 주어를 잃지 않기
grammar.summary: -ing, p.p., having p.p. 분사절은 이유·시간·결과를 간결하게 연결합니다. 생략된 주어가 주절의 주어와 일치해야 합니다.

points.title: Present participle
points.explanation: 같은 주어가 능동적으로 하는 동시·연속 행동을 -ing로 압축합니다.
examples: Reviewing the logs, we found a mismatch.
Using the checklist, the team caught two errors.

points.title: Past participle
points.explanation: 주어가 수동적으로 영향을 받은 상태를 과거분사로 표현합니다.
examples: Designed for beginners, the guide uses plain language.
Compared with the old model, the new one uses less memory.

points.title: Perfect participle
points.explanation: 분사절 행동이 먼저 완료됐음을 having + p.p.로 나타냅니다.
examples: Having reviewed the data, we reran the analysis.
Having been trained on mixed devices, the model generalized better.

points.title: Dangling modifier
points.explanation: 분사절의 숨은 주어가 주절 주어와 다르면 의미가 잘못 연결됩니다.
examples: Wrong: Driving to work, the rain became heavier.
Better: Driving to work, I noticed the rain getting heavier.

idioms.example: Your diagnosis was spot on.
Let's go over the checklist.
Small errors can fall through the cracks.
We need to tie up loose ends.
At first glance, the files look identical.

readingTitle: The Checklist That Caught a Silent Data Error
paragraphs: Preparing a multi-site imaging study, a research team copied files from three hospitals into one analysis system. At first glance, the import looked successful: the study count matched the plan and no files were reported as corrupted. Reviewing a small sample, however, an engineer noticed identical acquisition times across sites.

Going over the import logs, she found that one export tool had converted local time to UTC while another had not. The pixels were unchanged, so the model still ran, but the study protocol used timestamps to connect repeated examinations. Left uncorrected, the mismatch could link a follow-up scan to the wrong visit.

Having identified the risk, the team stopped the pipeline and built a short validation checklist covering patient-code format, dates, device manufacturer, image dimensions, orientation metadata and duplicate identifiers. Scripts handled repetitive checks, while reviewers inspected only flagged cases. The process found missing orientation tags and several duplicate studies that a simple file-count check had missed.

After correcting the data, the researchers reran every check and preserved the original exports. They learned that quality control is not paperwork added after analysis. It is part of the evidence chain. A useful checklist prevents routine problems from falling through the cracks and gives experts more time to investigate unusual ones.
translations: 다기관 영상 연구를 준비하던 팀은 세 병원의 파일을 하나의 분석 시스템으로 복사했습니다. 처음에는 검사 수가 맞고 손상 파일도 없어 성공처럼 보였지만 표본 검토에서 서로 다른 기관의 촬영 시간이 동일한 이상 패턴이 발견됐습니다.
로그를 확인하자 한 기관은 시간을 UTC로 변환했고 다른 기관은 현지 시간을 유지했습니다. 픽셀은 바뀌지 않아 모델은 실행됐지만 시간으로 반복 검사를 연결하는 연구에서는 잘못된 방문과 연결될 위험이 있었습니다.
위험을 확인한 팀은 파이프라인을 멈추고 환자 코드, 날짜, 장비, 영상 크기, 방향 메타데이터, 중복 식별자를 검사하는 짧은 체크리스트를 만들었습니다. 자동 스크립트와 사람의 검토를 결합해 파일 수만으로는 보이지 않던 문제를 찾았습니다.
수정 후 모든 검사를 다시 수행하고 원본을 보존했습니다. 품질관리는 분석 뒤의 서류 작업이 아니라 근거 사슬의 일부이며, 좋은 체크리스트는 반복 오류를 미리 드러내 전문가의 시간을 보호합니다.

vocabulary.context: 원본과 변경 이력을 따라갈 수 있는

choices: To keep it usable under pressure

title: Daily English — 2026-09-10

grammar.title: Modal Deduction: 증거로 현재와 과거를 추론하기
grammar.summary: must, might/may/could, can't와 must have, might have, can't have를 사용해 증거에 따른 확실성의 정도를 표현합니다.

points.title: must
points.explanation: 현재 증거로 매우 강하게 추론할 때 씁니다.
examples: The server is silent; it must be offline.
She must know the procedure.

points.title: might/may/could
points.explanation: 여러 가능성 중 하나일 때 사용합니다.
examples: The delay might be caused by preprocessing.
The cable could be loose.

points.title: can't
points.explanation: 증거상 거의 불가능하다고 판단할 때 사용합니다.
examples: It can't be the new model; the old build is running.
That can't be the final result.

points.title: Past deduction
points.explanation: 과거 추론은 modal + have + p.p.를 사용합니다.
examples: The process must have restarted overnight.
The file might have been copied twice.

idioms.example: The numbers don't add up.
We ruled out a network issue.
A driver bug is a long shot, but check it.
The logs helped narrow down the cause.
Don't jump to conclusions before checking the trace.

readingTitle: The Investigation of a Model That Suddenly Slowed Down
paragraphs: A medical-imaging team noticed that an inference service had become almost twice as slow after a routine deployment. The model weights had not changed, so several engineers initially assumed that the network must be responsible. Yet network timing looked normal, and the slowdown appeared inside the GPU stage.

The team avoided jumping to conclusions. They compared the current container with the previous one and ruled out a model-file change. A profiler showed many small CPU-to-GPU transfers. Someone suggested the data loader might have changed; another engineer thought mixed precision could have been disabled.

The logs narrowed the possibilities. GPU memory usage was higher than usual and tensors were stored as float32. The earlier service had used automatic mixed precision. A configuration flag must have been omitted during deployment. The team restored the flag and latency returned close to its previous level.

During the review, they separated facts from deductions. ‘The weights are identical’ was verified. ‘The network must be slow’ had been an early inference and turned out to be wrong. The incident taught the team to state how certain each hypothesis is and to update it as evidence arrives.
translations: 의료영상 팀은 정기 배포 후 추론 서비스가 거의 두 배 느려진 것을 발견했습니다. 모델 가중치는 같아 처음에는 네트워크가 원인이라고 추정했지만 네트워크 시간은 정상이고 지연은 GPU 단계 안에서 나타났습니다.
팀은 성급히 결론내리지 않고 이전 컨테이너와 비교했습니다. 프로파일러는 많은 CPU→GPU 전송을 보여줬고 데이터 로더 변경이나 mixed precision 비활성화 가능성이 제기됐습니다.
로그를 통해 범위를 좁히자 GPU 메모리가 늘고 tensor가 float32였으며, 이전 서비스가 쓰던 automatic mixed precision 설정이 빠진 것으로 드러났습니다. 설정을 복원하자 지연도 회복됐습니다.
사후 검토에서는 검증된 사실과 추론을 분리했습니다. 같은 가중치는 사실이었지만 네트워크가 느릴 것이라는 추론은 틀렸습니다. 증거에 따라 확신 수준을 표현하고 갱신하는 습관이 중요했습니다.

quiz.question: The server is silent. It _____ be offline.
The cable _____ be loose; let's check.
It _____ be the new model; the old build is running.

grammar.title: Comparatives: 차이를 과장하지 않고 정밀하게 비교하기
grammar.summary: far, slightly, considerably, not nearly as, by far 같은 표현으로 차이의 크기를 정확히 전달합니다.

points.title: Degree modifiers
points.explanation: 비교급 앞에서 차이의 정도를 조절합니다.
examples: Model A is slightly faster than B.
The new pipeline is considerably more stable.

points.title: not nearly as
points.explanation: 두 대상의 차이가 매우 큼을 표현합니다.
examples: The smaller model is not nearly as memory-hungry as the baseline.
The result is not nearly as clear as it first appeared.

points.title: the + comparative
points.explanation: 두 변화가 연결될 때 the more..., the more...를 씁니다.
examples: The larger the batch, the more memory we need.
The earlier we validate, the easier the fix becomes.

points.title: by far
points.explanation: 최상급 차이가 압도적일 때 사용합니다.
examples: This was by far the fastest configuration.
It is by far the most expensive option.

idioms.example: The model is ahead of the pack on latency.
On balance, the smaller model is safer.
There is a trade-off between speed and accuracy.
It won by a mile on memory use.
The result must hold up on external data.

readingTitle: Why the Fastest Model Was Not the Best Choice
paragraphs: An AI team compared three models for an ultrasound workstation. Model A produced the highest accuracy, Model B was slightly less accurate but considerably faster, and Model C was by far the smallest. At first, the team expected to choose the most accurate model.

Deployment tests changed the discussion. Model A required much more GPU memory and occasionally delayed the user interface. Model B was not nearly as demanding and still met the clinical performance threshold. Model C was fastest on an older device but lost too much sensitivity on difficult cases.

The team created a weighted decision table covering accuracy, latency, memory, calibration and hardware coverage. The more they tested realistic workflows, the clearer the trade-offs became. A single benchmark could not represent the whole product experience.

On balance, they selected Model B. It was not the winner on every metric, but it held up across more devices and caused fewer workflow delays. The exercise reminded the team that ‘best’ is meaningful only after the decision criteria and constraints are defined.
translations: 초음파 워크스테이션용 세 모델을 비교했습니다. A는 정확도가 최고였고 B는 약간 낮지만 훨씬 빨랐으며 C는 가장 작았습니다. 처음에는 가장 정확한 모델을 선택할 것으로 예상했습니다.
배포 시험에서 A는 메모리를 훨씬 많이 쓰고 UI를 지연시켰습니다. B는 부담이 훨씬 적으면서 임상 성능 기준을 만족했고 C는 오래된 장치에서 빨랐지만 어려운 사례 민감도가 낮았습니다.
팀은 정확도, 지연, 메모리, 보정, 하드웨어 범위를 가중치 표로 비교했습니다. 실제 workflow를 시험할수록 trade-off가 분명해졌고 단일 benchmark로 전체 제품 경험을 설명할 수 없었습니다.
종합적으로 B를 선택했습니다. 모든 지표 1등은 아니지만 더 많은 장치에서 안정적이었습니다. ‘최고’라는 말은 기준과 제약을 먼저 정의해야 의미가 있다는 교훈입니다.

quiz.question: Model B is _____ faster than A.
A is not nearly _____ efficient as B.
_____ larger the batch, the more memory we need.
What does hold up mean here?
Main lesson?
choices: Best depends on criteria and constraints

title: Daily English — 2026-09-12

grammar.title: Cohesion: 문장 사이의 논리 관계를 보이게 만들기
grammar.summary: however, therefore, in contrast, moreover, nevertheless, whereas 등 연결 표현을 기능별로 선택해 보고서의 논리 구조를 선명하게 합니다.

points.title: Contrast
points.explanation: however, in contrast, whereas로 차이와 반대를 표시합니다.
examples: Accuracy improved; however, latency increased.
Model A uses more memory, whereas B is lighter.

points.title: Cause/result
points.explanation: therefore, consequently, as a result로 결과 관계를 표시합니다.
examples: The cache was disabled; therefore, latency rose.
Two labels were missing. As a result, the batch was excluded.

points.title: Addition
points.explanation: moreover, furthermore, in addition은 새 근거를 더합니다.
examples: The model was faster. Moreover, it used less memory.
In addition, calibration improved.

points.title: Concession
points.explanation: although, even though, nevertheless로 예상과 다른 결과를 연결합니다.
examples: Although accuracy improved, the release was delayed.
The sample was small; nevertheless, the pattern was consistent.

idioms.example: The report helped us connect the dots.
Accuracy alone doesn't tell the whole story.
Use data to back up the claim.
The model is faster; on the other hand, it is less accurate.
The evidence makes a case for another test.

readingTitle: Why a Clear Technical Report Changed a Difficult Meeting
paragraphs: A validation team entered a meeting with mixed results. Accuracy had improved, but one device showed higher latency and a small subgroup had wider confidence intervals. The first draft report listed findings chronologically, so readers struggled to see which facts supported which conclusion.

The author reorganized the report by question. First, she stated what had improved. However, she immediately separated the unresolved device issue. In contrast with the overall result, that device showed a repeated delay. Moreover, she linked the delay to profiler evidence rather than speculation.

The revised report did not make weak evidence stronger; it made the relationships visible. During the meeting, people could distinguish confirmed findings from limitations and proposed follow-up work. Consequently, the discussion moved from arguing about wording to deciding what additional test was needed.
Clear discourse markers helped the report tell the whole story without pretending every result pointed in the same direction. Cohesion is not decoration. It is a way of making reasoning inspectable.
translations: 검증팀은 혼합된 결과를 가지고 회의에 들어갔습니다. 정확도는 좋아졌지만 한 장치의 지연은 커졌고 작은 하위군의 신뢰구간은 넓었습니다. 첫 보고서는 시간순으로 나열돼 결론과 근거 관계가 잘 보이지 않았습니다.
작성자는 질문별로 재구성했습니다. 개선점을 먼저 쓰되 unresolved device 문제를 바로 분리했고, 전체 결과와 달리 특정 장치에서 지연이 반복됐다는 점을 profiler 근거와 연결했습니다.
수정된 보고서는 약한 근거를 강하게 만든 것이 아니라 관계를 보이게 했습니다. 회의에서 확인된 사실, 한계, 후속 검증을 구분할 수 있었고 논쟁은 추가 시험 결정으로 이동했습니다.
연결 표현은 모든 결과가 같은 방향인 척하지 않으면서 전체 이야기를 보여주었습니다. 응집성은 장식이 아니라 추론을 검토 가능하게 만드는 도구입니다.

quiz.question: The cache was disabled; _____, latency rose.
The model was faster. _____, it used less memory.
_____ the sample was small, the pattern was repeated.
Why was first draft hard to use?
Main lesson?
choices: Cohesion makes reasoning easier to inspect

title: Daily English — 2026-09-13

grammar.title: Ellipsis & Substitution: 반복은 줄이고 의미는 유지하기
grammar.summary: do so, one/ones, so/not, auxiliary ellipsis 등으로 이미 분명한 내용을 반복하지 않습니다. 참조가 모호하면 생략하지 않습니다.

points.title: Auxiliary ellipsis
points.explanation: 앞의 동사구를 반복하지 않고 조동사나 be만 남깁니다.
examples: I expected the model to improve, and it did.
The first site was stable, but the second wasn't.

points.title: do so
points.explanation: 앞 행동 전체를 다소 격식 있게 대신합니다.
examples: We can rerun the test, but doing so will take two hours.
Document the change before you do so.

points.title: one/ones and so/not
points.explanation: 가산 명사나 앞 절의 내용을 대신합니다.
examples: The smaller scanner is newer than the one in Lab A.
Will the patch work? I think so.

points.title: Neither/so + auxiliary
points.explanation: 상대의 긍정·부정 경험에 동의할 때 도치합니다.
examples: I haven't seen it. — Neither have I.
The device needs calibration, and so does the backup unit.

idioms.example: Let's cut to the chase.
For labels, less is more.
Keep it simple.
You don't need to repeat yourself.
The shorter text gets the message across.

readingTitle: The Dashboard That Improved After Half Its Text Was Removed
paragraphs: A team built a monitoring dashboard for an AI service used by clinics. The first version explained every metric beside every chart. The information was accurate, but staff found it exhausting to scan and struggled to locate urgent status information.

During usability sessions, users mainly looked for service availability, processing delay and error rates. The design team cut to the chase. It grouped related metrics, defined repeated terms once, and used shorter references only when readers could clearly recover the omitted meaning.

The team worried that less text might reduce safety, so it tested both versions. Clinicians completed scenarios faster with the shorter dashboard and were no more likely to miss the escalation rule. Repeated instructions were easier to remember when placed once in a consistent location.

The lesson was not that less text is always better. Unusual failures still need full instructions. Repetition should be removed only when context remains unambiguous. The main dashboard became concise while a separate help page kept the detailed explanations.
translations: 여러 병원이 쓰는 AI 서비스 대시보드의 첫 버전은 모든 차트 옆에 모든 지표 설명을 반복했습니다. 정보는 정확했지만 긴급 상태를 빠르게 찾기 어려웠습니다.
사용자는 주로 서비스 가용성, 처리 지연, 오류율을 찾았습니다. 팀은 관련 지표를 묶고 반복 용어는 한 번만 정의했으며 생략 의미를 확실히 복원할 수 있을 때만 짧게 표현했습니다.
글을 줄이면 안전성이 낮아질까 시험했지만 임상의는 짧은 버전에서 더 빨리 과제를 수행했고 escalation 규칙 누락도 늘지 않았습니다. 반복 지침을 한 곳에 일관되게 둔 것이 도움이 됐습니다.
적은 글이 항상 좋다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 모호하면 전체 표현을 유지해야 합니다. 메인 화면은 간결하게 하고 상세 설명은 별도 도움말에 두었습니다.

quiz.question: Rerunning is possible, but _____ will take two hours.
The smaller scanner is newer than the _____.
I haven't seen it. — _____ have I.
Did shorter dashboard reduce test safety?
Main lesson?
choices: Remove repetition only when clarity remains
